## 固定收益市場主線

美國公債延續反彈，油價下跌減輕通膨補償，科技股盤中走弱也支撐公債需求。10年期殖利率下降3.85個基點至5.0683%，30年期下降4.81個基點至5.4099%；2年期則幾乎持平，收在4.8042%。漲勢主要集中在較長天期，對聯準會接下來幾次決策最敏感的短天期債券表現有限。

本日訊息進一步確認聯準會持續緊縮的意向，但官員對升息速度仍有分歧。10月會議紀錄顯示，幾乎所有與會者都預期還要升息。Christopher Waller認為，除非決策官員能可信地預告連續升息25個基點，否則12月可能需要升息50個基點；Mary Daly則支持以審慎步調進一步收緊政策。能源價格回落讓長天期債券喘息，政策辯論仍使短期借款成本承壓。

信用市場的改善較具選擇性。美國高收益債利差變動不大，Proofpoint則以較有利條件完成近$20億融資。在倫敦的信用市場會議上，放款機構與資產管理人談到再融資壓力升高、AI投資爭奪資金，以及個別借款人的投資機會。日本20年期公債標售需求疲弱、印尼意外升息，也分別提醒市場：美債上漲之際，全球融資環境仍未一致轉鬆。

## 油價回落帶動美債曲線趨平，聯準會討論升息步調

美債漲勢在午間前後加速，當時原油下跌，美股一度再創盤中低點。Bloomberg盤中報導指出，Waller上午的鷹派發言曾短暫壓抑債市，之後投資人重新評估能源降價對通膨的影響，帶動債券回升。TD Securities策略師Molly Brooks將改善歸因於市場對油價傳導至未來通膨數據的疑慮減輕；Westpac的Damien McColough也認為，價格已反映相當程度的升息風險。

收盤曲線反映出近期政策仍偏緊、較長天期債券則獲得支撐的差異。5年期殖利率下降2.7個基點至4.8877%，2年期微升0.01個基點。2年與10年期利差收窄3.86個基點至26.41個基點，2年與30年期利差縮減4.82個基點至60.57個基點。市場持續預期政策利率走高，長端反彈幅度仍較大。

10年期殖利率下降主要來自通膨補償減少：損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點至2.1976%，實質殖利率下降0.85個基點至2.8707%。不過，實質殖利率較一週前仍高10.04個基點，同期損益兩平通膨率下降2.17個基點；相較一個月前，兩者分別上升14.87個基點與下降15.32個基點。這使10年期名目殖利率僅較一個月前低0.45個基點，其背後的實質融資成本已明顯提高。

週三反彈後，名目殖利率仍高於一週前：2年期上升6.65個基點，10年期上升7.87個基點，30年期上升5.75個基點。依Bloomberg市場報導，指標美債在前一週因通膨遭到拋售後，已連續第三個交易日上漲。

WTI期貨收在每桶$83.26，下跌3.20%；布蘭特期貨收在$91.95，下跌1.28%。兩者分別較一個月前低約16%及14%。美國最新一週原油庫存增加340萬桶，汽油庫存增加500萬桶，其他煉製油品庫存也上升。CIBC Private Wealth的Rebecca Babin表示，交易員關注油市在10月轉為供給過剩，以及2027年庫存可能進一步累積。Energy Aspects Quant Analytics指出，主觀操作投資人退場後，即使規模不大的系統性賣盤也能推動價格。

波斯灣供給疑慮仍在。初步船舶追蹤資料顯示，荷姆茲海峽通行量可能較前月減少，但這項變化的意義尚不明朗。這些疑慮與庫存增加、買盤意願低迷並存。最新原油交易報導另指出，獲利了結、年底流動性轉薄及美元走強，也對油價構成壓力。

美元指數上升0.36%至103.86，黃金期貨下跌3.17%至每盎司$3,741.90。倫敦、紐約及上海銅價也大幅下挫；Bloomberg報導，投資人解除與AI題材相關的看多部位，LME銅價盤中最多下跌5.6%，觸及4月以來低點。標普500指數收跌0.23%，但那斯達克100指數和半導體指數回升，分別收漲0.42%及0.10%。VIX下降3.54%至24.56，仍較一週前高40.42%。

美國財政部20年期公債標售得標殖利率為5.459%，與紐約下午1時投標截止前的市場殖利率相同，比上月標售結果低1個基點。自標售公告以來，該債券殖利率一度升至5.54%，因此盤中債市回升對政府最終借款成本有實質影響。

下午2時公布的聯準會會議紀錄，進一步說明10月維持利率不變決定背後的緊縮傾向。委員會以10票對2票將目標區間維持在3.75%至4.00%；當次具有投票權的理事Lisa Cook與克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack主張升息25個基點。幾乎所有與會者依其通膨與勞動市場基準展望，都預期還需升息；少數與會者認為，若通膨數據不利，下次會議可能適合升息超過25個基點。

溝通方式是分歧的重要一環。部分原本傾向10月升息的與會者，只要市場清楚理解後續很可能繼續緊縮，也能接受暫停升息。在支持等待的官員中，有幾位認為市場預期12月及2027年升息，大致符合適當政策方向，因此立即維持利率的風險較小。其他官員則希望取得更多有關AI投資、融資環境、9月升息傳導及地緣政治發展的證據。

Waller週三接受CNBC訪問時，進一步闡述這項政策訊號問題。他指出，最近三個月通膨年化速度接近3.5%，明顯高於2%目標。若要以兩次各25個基點達到所需緊縮程度，12月就必須可信地表明1月還會再升息；缺乏這項訊號時，他傾向考慮12月一次升息50個基點。Waller曾支持10月按兵不動，這次發言反映其評估持續演變，與10月的反對票立場有所區別。

Daly在聖路易聯準銀行會議上提出不同的政策偏好。她表示，仍須進一步緊縮，才能確信通膨正逐步朝2%回落；但關稅、伊朗戰爭與AI投資的不確定性，意味著行動應審慎、有節奏，並參考經濟數據及與企業、消費者的交流。理事Michael Barr另表示，調高利率可能是適當做法。週三期貨市場報導仍顯示，市場預期12月與1月各升息25個基點，4月前再升息一次。

住宅數據反映借款成本對市場各環節的影響不一。10月新屋開工增加9.9%，年率為130.9萬戶，高於市場共識125萬戶及修正後前值119.1萬戶。多戶住宅開工增加近24%，獨棟住宅增加4%至86.4萬戶。中西部與南部營建活動增強，南部達4月以來最強，西部開工則降至逾六年低點。

後續建案動能轉弱。建築許可初值下降7.4%至129.5萬戶，低於前值139.8萬戶及Trading Economics共識138萬戶，為2020年5月以來最低；獨棟住宅許可降至2023年以來最低。Pantheon Macroeconomics的Olivia Cross預期，未來六個月建商將減少新案，原因包括房貸利率偏高使需求疲弱，以及開發商債券與銀行貸款成本上升。開工估計本身波動也大，政府公布的月變動90%信賴區間介於下降6.9%至增加26.7%。

全美不動產經紀人協會（NAR）另一份報告顯示，10月成屋待完成銷售下降4.7%，指數降至63，創2001年開始統計以來最低，並較去年同期低約17%。各區簽約量均下降，以西部減少6.9%、南部減少6.3%最明顯。NAR經濟學家Lawrence Yun表示，若房貸利率已見頂，10月可能就是本輪簽約量的低點。待完成購屋交易再度萎縮，加上許可減少，顯示實際開工雖回升，住宅市場整體仍承受沉重融資壓力。

## Proofpoint順利定價，信用風險走向分歧

Thoma Bravo旗下資安公司Proofpoint完成近$20億融資，需求強勁讓債券與貸款條件同步改善。知情人士表示，摩根大通牽頭的銀行將$12.5億債券定價於8.5%殖利率，低於初步討論的9%區間低端，認購訂單超過$60億。

配套的$7.35億貸款以面額定價，利率為基準加4.5個百分點，取消先前最低曾至面額99.27%的折價。債券用於支持收購Varonis，貸款則完成自7月展開的再融資，並可與公司既有定期貸款合併流通。Thoma Bravo也提供收購股本，安大略省教師退休基金已同意投資。貸款發行價格改善降低了融資成本，約定的基準加碼利率並未改變。

此前，CCC Intelligent Solutions的$28.5億收購融資案需求也增強，訂單已超過$100億。巴克萊另正為CVR Energy收購Marathon Petroleum煉油廠，安排出售約$25億債務。Qualtrics約$50億貸款的分銷仍較困難，摩根大通牽頭的銀行團可能以大幅折價出售部分貸款，以降低自身曝險。

這些不同結果，呼應週三Bloomberg全球信用論壇的討論。KKR的Eddie O’Neill估計，美國與歐洲槓桿貸款及高收益債的困境債務比率約為8%至9%，預期融資成本升高將增加財務困境，並使績效明顯分化。Song Jin Lee所領導的匯豐策略團隊則認為，以偏高槓桿倍數承作的中型企業私人放貸風險更大。他們預期公開市場高收益債較有韌性，因為CCC級債務占比較低，到期安排也提供較充裕的再融資時間。

其他經理人則在賣壓後看到個別投資機會。J.P. Morgan Asset Management的Iain Stealey判斷，多數BB級與B級企業仍健全，並偏好較強的投資級發行人所發行的次順位債權。MFS的Pilar Gomez-Bravo指出，個別較低評級及次順位證券出現價格失衡，包括註冊於法國的全球企業。相對於市場對最弱借款人的擔憂，兩人的看法更強調企業品質與資本結構的差異。

全日美國高收益債利差變動不大。計入配息後，LQD報酬率為0.40%，HYG則上漲0.03%。美債上漲伴隨投資級債較佳的報酬，個別借款人的融資條件仍持續分化。

AI融資仍是爭奪資本的重要來源。Polus Capital Management的Robert Dafforn認為，放款審核品質已惡化，列舉槓桿提高、獲利與現金流走弱、股本緩衝偏薄，以及以較缺乏實體形態的資產作為放款依據等問題。Bloomberg估計，自2025年以來，全球為AI建設所借入的資金已超過$8,200億。Dafforn預期，這類融資需求會使其他產業更難再融資，並促成債務重整。Davidson Kempner的Chris Krishanthan則看好股本與債務配置適當的機會，以及銀行年底前暫時需要降低資產負債表負擔時所釋出的交易。

新研究顯示科技公司的投資組成正在改變。聖路易聯準銀行研究人員Julian Kozlowski、Juan Sánchez與Nicholas Sullivan發現，大型雲端業者資本支出占資產比率，從2018年初約5%升至2026年初近13%；研發支出占比則從2023年初約11%的高峰降至9.3%。現金占資產比率由2018年約34%降至今年16%，平均僅比其他企業高約5個百分點。這些歷史比較量化了實體投資比重增加，以及現金相對資產減少的變化。

Nvidia財報公布後初期的漲勢未能延續，正常交易時段收跌2.9%。代理執行長Colette Kress表示，未來對AI生態系的投資將更有紀律，並接受更嚴格審視。儘管已取得美國許可，公司仍停止向中國出貨獲准出口的Hopper資料中心晶片。知情人士透露，獵才人員曾接觸Arm執行長Rene Haas，洽詢Nvidia最高主管職位。投資人因此同時評估設備需求，以及Nvidia下一任領導團隊將提供多少客戶融資支持。

Anthropic的IPO從推介進展至傳出定價。知情人士表示，每股定價為$83，高於$70至$78的區間。Bloomberg亞洲早盤報導稱，預期募資至少$680億，若計入$260億私募則超過$940億，並指出發行規模擴大。在預期掛牌交易前，這項定價結果已帶來重大的股權融資進展，而供應運算能力的成本仍是公司長期經營效益的核心。

另一筆私人市場交易中，放款機構提供$13億貸款，供L Catterton收購醫療保健平台Fullscript，使摩根士丹利牽頭的銀行團解除承銷承諾。咖啡機製造商Evoca債務負擔增加，Carlyle與Park Square Capital將接手公司。兩案用途不同：前者替換收購融資，後者則涉及控制權可能轉移至債權人。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，Scientific Games的消息呈現另一種鮮明的個別借款人差異。放款機構取得較完整的獲利與現金資訊後，該公司$8億無擔保債券週三每1美元面額上漲3美分至36美分，$21億定期貸款則大致持平於面額75%。知悉數據的人士表示，這家Brookfield旗下彩票企業截至9月季度營收為$2.68億，下降10%；調整後EBITDA為$7,300萬，下降近32%。部分落差源自合約延後相關的$1,300萬一次性調整。公司動用循環信用額度$4,000萬回購債券，另有$4,400萬受限制現金及$3.59億循環信用額度。營運數字惡化之際，資訊更清楚仍支撐了困境債務價格。

## 歐洲面臨升息需求與金融市場脆弱性

歐洲央行副總裁Boris Vujcic對未來通膨擴散提出更明確的判斷。他表示，若無意外，12月升息的可能性很高；隨著第二輪效應遞延浮現，明年價格壓力將擴散至能源以外。他認為市場預期2027年繼續緊縮屬合理，但仍須逐次會議決定。在通膨約為歐洲央行2%目標兩倍之際，這番評估更強調能源成本接下來的傳導。

歐洲央行《金融穩定評論》另指出，主權債務的持有結構與融資方式存在脆弱性。避險基金有助吸收發債供給並改善流動性，但對價格及融資條件敏感，可能放大殖利率急變，即使主權基本面沒有改變也可能發生。Vujcic表示，歐洲市場由五家大型業者主導，並舉例說明避險基金快速交易曾使利差擴大，之後市場才恢復正常。

評論也討論科技公司在股價指數權重提高後，AI曝險日益增加的問題。Vujcic表示，股市若大幅修正，將使歐洲個人消費下降1個百分點。他認為銀行憑藉獲利、資本及流動性，具備良好承受衝擊能力，同時提醒部分非銀行機構存在流動性與槓桿弱點。銀行資產負債表的韌性，與市場型金融可能出現的不穩定並存。

德國正式提名普林斯頓大學經濟學家Markus Brunnermeier接替Isabel Schnabel，出任歐洲央行執行理事，推進本週稍早討論的人事方案。柏林希望他在Philip Lane任期於5月結束後接掌首席經濟學家職務。執政聯盟的安排也為德國支持Pablo Hernandez de Cos出任總裁鋪路，法國亦支持這項人選。德國政府表示，將持續在歐盟內討論，目標是年底前完成人事任命。Christine Lagarde另確認將留任總裁至2月7日，並表示世界經濟論壇職務是之後的可能選項之一。

歐洲保險業的信用融資能力，面臨另一項結構性變化。標普全球評級估計，1月30日生效的Solvency II修訂，可能就既有持倉釋出€800億監理資本。Blackstone、Apollo等管理機構正爭取資產約€10兆的歐盟保險業配置，尤其是CLO、私人投資級債務及其他證券化投資。

新制降低部分私募股權與優先順位結構型信用投資的資本要求，某些情況降幅超過一半。合格長期股權持倉的資本計提率可為22%，相較之下，一般上市股票為39%，多數私募股權及其他未上市投資為49%。另一套證券化方案已就部分架構的優先順位部位達成初步協議，將銀行風險權數下限由10%降至5%。

實際配置仍取決於投資授權、專業能力、盡職調查，以及低流動性資產與保險負債的配合。部分最大型保險公司使用內部模型計算資本要求，特定修訂的直接影響因而有限。MetLife Investment Management的Laila Kollmorgen指出，CLO占美國壽險投資組合15%，歐盟保險公司的各類證券化資產合計則不到1%。依AFME資料，截至6月底歐洲證券化商品流通餘額接近€1.3兆，年增2.7%。

監理機關質疑，清償能力比率背後的資本保障將會減少。EIOPA主席Petra Hielkema警告，看似相近的比率可能由較少的實際資本支撐，並表示資本鬆綁並非為了單純向股東或管理階層發放款項。美國AI融資的競爭也可能使資金轉離歐洲項目。Apollo的Diego De Giorgi估計，歐洲每年投資需求為€1.4兆，高於Draghi報告的€8,000億，並強調除大型企業外，國防與科技供應鏈也需要融資。

Alstom最新財務結構更新，顯示個別發行人更迫切的限制。公司希望在2027年9月前減債約€20億以保住投資級評等，但已下修資產出售預期，使分析師更預期公司會辦理現金增資。管理階層排除出售主要號誌業務，也認為服務與合資事業具有策略重要性。花旗分析師預期將有相當部分資金來自股本，最高可能達€15億。股價盤中最多下跌9.6%。德國列車專案延誤與成本超支壓迫現金流，擬議融資組合仍在評估中。

英國住宅市場呈現高融資成本的另一項影響。官方9月數據顯示，內倫敦房價年跌7.2%至£621,491，為2009年8月以來最大跌幅；整個倫敦下跌3.5%。西敏市下跌18.5%，肯辛頓與切爾西下跌15.6%，全國則上漲1.2%。Savills的Lucian Cook將內倫敦的敏感度歸因於偏高的房價所得比，高價房產稅負又增加壓力。另一方面，依Bloomberg報導，英國通膨大致符合市場共識、但低於英格蘭銀行預測，英國公債週三表現優於美債；該報導所述時段的2年期殖利率下降逾6個基點至4.92%。

## 日本標售反映超長天期公債需求受限

投資人權衡利率波動與政府融資計畫，日本20年期公債標售需求轉弱。投標倍數從前次5.84倍降至3.64倍，低於過去12個月平均3.92倍；平均得標價格與最低得標價格的差距，由0.07擴至0.29，為一年來最大。20年期殖利率當日仍下降3個基點至3.74%，但11月至今仍上升逾20個基點。

法巴資產管理策略師Ryutaro Kimura表示，利率波動使風險承受意願下降，壓抑投資人買進超長債的意願。他預期投資人將等待12月預算提案，以釐清下個會計年度發債規模。提高國防支出及擬議為期兩年的食品消費稅調降所需融資，仍是供給的重要不確定因素。

財政制度等審議會的建議草案指出，債務平均期限較長，且有大量低票息債券，使利率上升尚需時間才會完全反映在利息支出，但也敦促政府在衝擊到來前整頓財政。財務省已為下個會計年度申請創紀錄的¥16.6兆利息支出預算。該委員會要求持續改善債務永續性，並反對以新增借款支應國防擴張。其警告關乎政府投資計畫能否維持所需的市場信心。

日本央行總裁植田和男維持進一步升息的立場，前提是經濟、通膨與金融情勢支持。對於擬議食品稅調降，他表示實質購買力提高可能支持成長，但對基礎通膨的影響取決於企業定價與家庭行為。政策細節確定後，日本央行會納入評估。

植田也區分兩類操作：為處理嚴重市場功能失靈而緊急買債，以及以壓低長期殖利率為目的的操作。他警告，投資人可能將壓抑殖利率視為以貨幣融通政府支出，反使長債殖利率波動加劇。在日本央行持續推動政策正常化之際，這項區分為標售與財政討論劃出重要的貨幣政策界線。

10月貿易數據帶來外需支撐與進口成本壓力的新訊息。出口年增20.5%，高於路透共識20.0%及9月16.5%，名目金額創紀錄、接近¥11.8兆。對美國出口增加23.9%，對中國增加13.3%，半導體相關AI需求有所貢獻。經濟學家也指出，售價提高與成本轉嫁推升了名目成長。

進口增加21.6%，低於預期25.8%，金額創紀錄、接近¥12.2兆，數量則減少約0.2%。貿易逆差為¥4,765億，低於預期¥9,560億。偏高的原油與運輸成本，是進口支出增加的部分原因。因此，逆差小於預期及出口收入強勁的同時，能源成本負擔仍在，近期國內消費疲弱也仍影響日本央行的成長評估。

## 匯率防衛與公共融資各有難題

印尼央行升息25個基點至6%，為6月以來首次升息；Bloomberg最終調查的38位經濟學家中，有22位原先預期維持不變。總裁Destry Damayanti表示，此舉旨在穩定印尼盾，並預先確保通膨留在1.5%至3.5%目標區間。決策後印尼盾微升不到0.1%，至每美元18,238印尼盾，10年期公債殖利率則延續升勢至7.75%。

央行升息之際，也進一步調降部分境內無本金交割遠期外匯的避險溢價，並計畫最遲於3月推出跨幣別附買回交易，讓銀行以合格的印尼央行美元證券取得流動性。Destry表示，除較緊的政策利率外，降低存款準備率與總體審慎誘因將支持實體經濟融資。

Danamon的Irman Faiz指出，信用成長超過13%，其中消費貸款增加4.7%，顯示經濟仍有韌性。他預測12月再升息25個基點至6.25%，之後維持至2027年底。第三季GDP年增約5.5%。美元走強、MSCI的降級警告及國內政治不確定性，使匯率承壓，央行因而須在匯率穩定與成長間取捨。

南非新公布的通膨數據，使相同的政策取捨更為複雜。10月消費者通膨由4.5%加速至5.2%，符合Bloomberg調查中位數，核心通膨由4%升至4.2%。黃金下跌，加上市場預期聯準會升息、威脅南非的利差優勢，蘭特盤中最多貶值1.9%，降至3月以來最低。指標10年期公債殖利率上升約9個基點至8.91%，為四週高點。

多數受訪經濟學家仍預期南非儲備銀行週四將利率維持在7.25%。Ninety One的James Turp認為，通膨高於預期的程度尚不足以要求緊縮，但也承認核心數據更強。南非財政與金融委員會另說明一套擬議架構，要求歷屆政府提出可信的中期財政計畫，接受獨立評估並向國會負責。這套以原則為基礎的制度，將透過三年規劃期推動持久財政整頓，而不採固定債務上限。

智利經濟成長受挫更深。第三季GDP季減1.8%，差於預期下降1.4%，年減1.1%。礦業季減12.9%，其他經濟部門合計下降0.2%。央行將第二季成長率由略為負值、四捨五入為零，修正為0.1%。這使先前衰退說法所依據的季度成長軌跡有所改變。

惡劣天候干擾礦場與運輸，失業及燃料成本也壓抮信心。Pantheon Macroeconomics的Andrés Abadía預期，明年復甦很大部分來自有利的比較基期，礦石品位下降及投資疲弱仍限制礦業。通膨為4.5%，高於3%目標。國會本週批准延續至4月的燃料價格上限，在產出走弱、成本偏高之際，新增一項政策回應。

依墨西哥永續金融委員會資料，主權永續債務發行達1,693億披索，約合$91億，較2025年全年增加79%，創2020年首次發行此類公債以來紀錄。資產約$5,000億的退休基金是重要買家。新揭露要求鼓勵永續報告，但未強制基金購買ESG證券。

需求帶來的好處比穩定的定價優勢更明確。Bloomberg比較兩組同幣別、同到期年度的永續與一般債券，發現永續債殖利率一組高5個基點，另一組高1個基點。VALMEX的Yazmín Matus表示，優勢在於認購量。稍早合計350億披索的永續固定與浮動利率債發行，投標倍數為2.6倍，另一筆90億披索Udibonos發行則為1.7倍。

花旗的Miguel Azevedo預測，2027年非洲主權美元債交易筆數將超過今年迄今創紀錄的25筆。Bloomberg資料顯示，九個國家透過發行歐洲債券籌得$169億；非洲企業不含開發銀行，則透過89筆發行籌得近$100億。Azevedo將未來發行動能歸因於總體經濟穩定改善與改革，IMF預測撒哈拉以南非洲今年及明年成長率均為4.5%。這個在全球動盪中仍保有融資管道的市場，依他的預測，明年發行將更活躍。

肯亞揭露的融資款項用途則受到更多限制。財政部長John Mbadi表示，Vodacom增購Safaricom股權及未來股利證券化所得的大部分資金，在上訴期間投資於政府債券與國庫券。兩項交易分別籌得2,043億及402億肯亞先令。高等法院兩個月前裁定，新增出售的20%股權須交還財政部，案件目前由上訴法院審理。Mbadi表示，上訴法院未禁止動用資金，但財政部警告，爭議威脅到原定作為國家基礎建設基金資本的款項。

美國市政債方面，Bloomberg新分析顯示，德州選民本月否決至少$70億債券提案，其中至少$60億用於學校。Collin County的$8.17億方案遭否決，儘管支應方案的稅率原本不需調高；官員表示，選票上警告增稅的文字可能是原因之一。Bexar County選民否決San Antonio獨立學區的$6億方案及約3美分的房產稅調升。學區表示，未來校舍整修或重建取決於債券最終獲准，而入學人數減少及結構性預算赤字已限制財務。Plano選民否決場館稅，也迫使相關方面重新評估Dallas Stars球場的擬議融資。

## 後續市場關注

Anthropic預期11月19日開始交易，在傳出每股$83定價與募資擴大後，將檢驗公開市場需求。Nvidia財報帶來的反彈已消退，投資人也在衡量產業運算成本及債務、股權融資能力，眼前焦點是Anthropic掛牌後的股價表現。供應商的投資紀律與融資實際進度，將分別影響基礎設施擴張速度。

南非週四政策決策前，通膨已達5.2%，核心通膨上升，匯率再度承壓。若如預期將利率維持在7.25%，央行將在評估匯率效應與油價下降之際，依靠現有緊縮程度。印尼意外升息後，下次決策的起點不同；國內信用韌性與印尼盾能否持續穩定，將是是否進一步緊縮的關鍵。

12月8日至9日FOMC會議面臨的升息步調與溝通選擇已更明確。Waller提出將50個基點分兩次調整的條件，使1月指引的可信度成為後續通膨之外的另一項考量。Daly主張審慎步調，則更重視投資、關稅與戰爭的不確定性。接下來的通膨數據，將決定官員支持進一步緊縮的立場，會轉化為立即較大幅升息，或連續較小幅升息。

日本12月預算提案，將揭示曾壓抑20年期標售需求的財政計畫，會如何影響發債。日本央行12月18日決策是另一項政策事件，植田對需求與基礎通膨的評估，關係到進一步正常化。歐洲領袖下週討論歐洲央行人事，將決定德國提名與政治支持能否形成獲得同意的領導層方案。

美國10月建築許可終值預定11月25日格林威治時間13時公布，Trading Economics所列共識為129.5萬戶。開工回升、待完成購屋交易減少後，這項數據將再度檢視許可初值所呈現的未來建案大幅收縮。另方面，深圳峰會外交對科技取得與區域安全的影響仍未定。任何涉及先進運算或能源運輸的具體協議，都將改變目前仍受政策限制與實體供給風險影響的融資假設。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌帶動較長天期美債反彈，聯準會升息預期未退
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債延續反彈，油價回落減輕通膨補償，科技股盤中走弱也支撐公債需求。10年期殖利率下降3.85個基點至5.0683%，30年期下降4.81個基點至5.4099%；2年期微升0.01個基點至4.8042%。2年與10年期利差收窄3.86個基點至26.41個基點。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點，是名目殖利率下滑的主要來源，實質殖利率另下降0.85個基點。實質融資成本仍高於一週及一個月前。

聯準會10月會議紀錄顯示，幾乎所有與會者都預期還要升息。Christopher Waller認為，除非政策指引能可信地預告連續升息25個基點，否則12月可能需要升息50個基點；Mary Daly則支持以審慎步調進一步緊縮。原油庫存增加有助減輕能源價格壓力，政策辯論仍讓短期借款成本維持高檔。

美國高收益債利差變動不大，Proofpoint以較佳條件完成近$20億融資。信用市場經理人指出，再融資壓力正增加，AI投資也在爭奪資金。日本20年期公債標售需求疲弱，印尼意外升息至6%，顯示各市場融資環境仍不一致。
overall_summary.summary: 通膨補償下降與科技股盤中走弱支撐公債，近期政策仍偏緊，使2年期殖利率幾乎持平；信用融資的改善則較具選擇性。

section_summaries.summary: 美債反彈仍集中在較長天期，對聯準會接下來幾次決策最敏感的短天期債券漲勢有限。油價回落降低通膨補償，科技股盤中走弱支撐公債，決策官員則進一步確認持續緊縮的必要。Proofpoint取得較佳融資條件，但再融資壓力、日本疲弱標售及印尼意外升息，使全球情勢仍不一致。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their recovery as falling oil prices eased inflation compensation and intraday weakness in technology shares supported demand for government debt. The 10-year yield declined 3.85 basis points to 5.0683%, while the 30-year fell 4.81 basis points to 5.4099%. The two-year finished virtually unchanged at 4.8042%, leaving the rally concentrated beyond the maturities most sensitive to the next Federal Reserve decisions.

The session brought stronger evidence of the Fed's commitment to further tightening alongside disagreement about its speed. October's minutes revealed that almost all participants anticipated more increases, and Christopher Waller argued that a half-point December move could be necessary unless policymakers credibly signaled consecutive quarter-point steps. Mary Daly supported further restraint at a measured pace. Cheaper energy gave longer bonds relief while that policy debate kept pressure on short-term borrowing costs.

Credit markets showed a more selective recovery. U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed, and Proofpoint completed nearly $2 billion of financing on improved terms. At a London credit gathering, lenders and managers described growing refinancing pressure, competing demands from AI investment and opportunities in individual borrowers. Japan's weak 20-year auction and Indonesia's unexpected rate increase supplied separate reminders that the U.S. duration rally was not a uniform easing of global financing conditions.

## Oil Relief Flattens Treasuries as the Fed Debates Pace

The Treasury rally gathered momentum around midday as crude fell and U.S. stocks temporarily reached new session lows. Bloomberg's intraday account described a brief setback in bonds after Waller's hawkish morning remarks, followed by gains as investors reassessed the inflation consequences of cheaper energy. TD Securities strategist Molly Brooks attributed the improvement to reduced concern about oil passing through into future inflation readings. Westpac's Damien McColough also argued that considerable rate-increase risk was already reflected in prices.

The closing curve captured the separation between near-term policy restraint and longer-duration relief. Five-year yields declined 2.7 basis points to 4.8877%, while the two-year edged up 0.01 basis point. The two- to 10-year gap narrowed 3.86 basis points to 26.41 basis points, and the two- to 30-year spread contracted 4.82 basis points to 60.57. The longer end recovered more strongly as the market continued to expect higher policy rates.

Inflation compensation accounted for most of the 10-year decline. The breakeven fell 3 basis points to 2.1976%, while the real yield eased 0.85 basis point to 2.8707%. Over the week, however, the real yield remained 10.04 basis points higher, against a 2.17-basis-point reduction in the breakeven. The corresponding monthly changes were a 14.87-basis-point rise in real yields and a 15.32-basis-point decline in inflation compensation. That combination left nominal 10-year yields only 0.45 basis point below their month-earlier level, with a materially higher real financing cost underneath.

The weekly rise in nominal yields also survived Wednesday's rally: the two-year remained 6.65 basis points higher, the 10-year 7.87 higher and the 30-year 5.75 higher. The recovery was the third consecutive session of gains for benchmark Treasuries in Bloomberg's market account, following the previous week's inflation-driven selloff.

WTI futures ended at $83.26 a barrel, down 3.20%, and Brent at $91.95, down 1.28%. They were about 16% and 14% below their month-earlier levels, respectively. U.S. crude inventories rose 3.4 million barrels in the latest week, while gasoline stocks increased 5 million barrels and other refined-product inventories also expanded. CIBC Private Wealth's Rebecca Babin said traders were concentrating on the transition to an October surplus and the prospect of further inventory accumulation in 2027. Energy Aspects Quant Analytics described a market in which even modest systematic selling was moving prices as discretionary investors withdrew.

Supply concerns remained active in the Persian Gulf. Preliminary vessel tracking suggested Hormuz transits were falling month on month, although the significance of the decline was unclear. Those concerns coexisted with the inventory build and weak buying appetite. The latest oil trading account described profit-taking, thinning year-end liquidity and a stronger dollar as additional pressures on crude.

The dollar index rose 0.36% to 103.86, and gold futures fell 3.17% to $3,741.90 an ounce. Copper also sold off sharply across London, New York and Shanghai; Bloomberg reported an intraday LME decline of as much as 5.6% to the lowest since April as investors abandoned AI-linked bullish positions. The S&P 500 finished down 0.23%, but the Nasdaq 100 and the semiconductor index recovered to close up 0.42% and 0.10%, respectively. The VIX eased 3.54% to 24.56, remaining 40.42% above its week-earlier level.

Treasury's 20-year auction cleared at 5.459%, matching the yield indicated immediately before the 1 p.m. New York bidding deadline. That was 1 basis point below the previous month's auction result. Bonds had traded as high as 5.54% since the sale was announced, making the intraday recovery consequential for the government's eventual borrowing rate.

The Fed minutes, released at 2 p.m., clarified how much tightening support lay behind October's unchanged decision. The committee voted 10-2 to hold the target range at 3.75%-4.00%; Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, both voters at that meeting, preferred a 25-basis-point increase. Almost all participants expected further increases under their baseline inflation and labor-market outlooks. A couple considered a move larger than 25 basis points at the next meeting potentially appropriate if inflation data were unfavorable.

Communication was an important part of the disagreement. Some participants who preferred an October increase could have accepted a hold if markets clearly understood that further tightening was likely. Among supporters of waiting, several regarded expected increases in December and 2027 as broadly consistent with appropriate policy, reducing the risk of leaving rates unchanged immediately. Others wanted more evidence on AI investment, financing conditions, the transmission of September's increase and geopolitical developments.

Waller's Wednesday CNBC interview developed that signaling issue. He put the annualized pace of inflation over the latest three months near 3.5%, well above the 2% objective. Two quarter-point moves could deliver the desired restraint, he argued, only if December brought a credible indication of another increase in January. Without that signal, he favored considering 50 basis points in December. He had backed October's hold, placing his latest remarks within an evolving assessment rather than the October dissenting bloc.

Daly offered a distinct policy preference at a St. Louis Fed conference. Further tightening was needed to establish confidence that inflation was moving gradually toward 2%, she said, but uncertainty over tariffs, the Iran war and AI investment warranted thoughtful, measured action informed by economic data and conversations with businesses and consumers. Governor Michael Barr separately said higher rates would likely be appropriate. Wednesday's futures accounts continued to describe expectations for quarter-point increases in December and January, with another by April.

Housing data exposed the uneven effects of those borrowing costs. October starts increased 9.9% to an annualized 1.309 million, above the 1.25 million consensus and a revised 1.191 million previously. Multifamily construction rose nearly 24%, while single-family starts increased 4% to 864,000. Construction strengthened in the Midwest and South, with the South at its strongest since April; starts in the West fell to their lowest in more than six years.

The prospective construction pipeline weakened. Preliminary permits fell 7.4% to 1.295 million, from 1.398 million and below Trading Economics' 1.38 million consensus, reaching the weakest level since May 2020. Single-family permits dropped to their lowest since 2023. Pantheon Macroeconomics' Olivia Cross expected builders to reduce new projects over the next six months, citing weak demand at elevated mortgage rates and higher bond and bank-loan costs for developers. The starts estimate was volatile: the government's 90% confidence interval for its monthly change ran from a 6.9% decline to a 26.7% increase.

A separate National Association of Realtors release showed October pending home sales falling 4.7% to an index level of 63, the lowest since records began in 2001, and about 17% below a year earlier. Contract signings declined in every region, led by the West's 6.9% fall and the South's 6.3% decline. NAR economist Lawrence Yun said October could mark the cycle's low in signings if mortgage rates had peaked. The fresh contraction in prospective purchases, alongside falling permits, left the rebound in actual construction concentrated in a housing market still under substantial financing pressure.

## Proofpoint Prices Successfully as Credit Risks Diverge

Proofpoint completed its near-$2 billion financing after demand allowed the Thoma Bravo-backed cybersecurity company to improve both bond and loan terms. JPMorgan-led banks priced the $1.25 billion bond at an 8.5% yield, down from initial discussions in the low-9% range. Orders exceeded $6 billion, according to people familiar with the transaction.

The accompanying $735 million loan priced at par with a margin of 4.5 percentage points over its benchmark, eliminating an earlier discount as low as 99.27 cents. The bond supports the Varonis acquisition, while the loan completes the refinancing effort begun in July and is fungible with the company's existing term loan. Thoma Bravo is also supplying acquisition equity, and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan has agreed to invest. The improved issue price reduced the loan's funding cost without changing its stated benchmark margin.

The financing followed stronger demand for CCC Intelligent Solutions' $2.85 billion acquisition package, where orders had now exceeded $10 billion. Barclays was separately working to sell about $2.5 billion of debt for CVR Energy's purchase of refineries from Marathon Petroleum. Distribution remained more difficult for roughly $5 billion of Qualtrics loans: the JPMorgan-led bank group could offer part at a significant discount to reduce its exposure.

Those different outcomes gave substance to Wednesday's discussion at Bloomberg's Global Credit Forum. KKR's Eddie O'Neill put the distressed ratio across U.S. and European leveraged loans and high-yield bonds near 8%-9%, expecting higher financing costs to create more distress and pronounced performance differences. HSBC strategists led by Song Jin Lee located the larger vulnerability in middle-market private lending extended at stretched leverage multiples. They expected public junk bonds to prove more resilient because triple-C debt forms a smaller share of that market and maturities provide a longer refinancing runway.

Other managers saw selective value after the selloff. J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Iain Stealey said most double-B and single-B companies remained healthy in his assessment, while favoring subordinated claims on stronger investment-grade issuers. MFS's Pilar Gomez-Bravo described dislocations in individual lower-rated and subordinated securities, including global companies domiciled in France. Their assessments contrasted with concern about the weakest borrowers and emphasized differences in business quality and capital structure.

For the session as a whole, U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed. LQD returned 0.40% including distributions, while HYG gained 0.03%. The stronger return in investment-grade debt accompanied the Treasury rally, even as borrower-specific financing terms continued to diverge.

AI funding remained a major source of competition for capital. Polus Capital Management's Robert Dafforn argued that underwriting quality had deteriorated, citing higher leverage, weaker earnings and cash flow, thin equity cushions and lending against less tangible assets. Bloomberg put worldwide borrowing for the AI buildout at more than $820 billion since 2025. Dafforn expected that demand for financing to make refinancing harder in other industries and contribute to restructurings. Davidson Kempner's Chris Krishanthan saw opportunities where the balance between equity and debt was appropriate, and where banks needed temporary balance-sheet relief before year-end.

Fresh research described a shift in the composition of technology-company investment. St. Louis Fed researchers Julian Kozlowski, Juan Sánchez and Nicholas Sullivan found that hyperscaler capital expenditure rose to almost 13% of assets in early 2026 from about 5% at the start of 2018. Research and development, by comparison, fell to 9.3% of assets from a peak near 11% in early 2023. Cash holdings declined to 16% of assets this year from about 34% in 2018, leaving them only about 5 percentage points above other companies on average. Those historical comparisons quantify the growing weight of physical investment and the reduction in cash relative to assets.

Nvidia's early post-earnings gains gave way to a 2.9% regular-session decline. Interim CEO Colette Kress said future investments across the AI ecosystem would face greater discipline and scrutiny. The company also stopped shipping licensed Hopper data-center chips to China despite U.S. permission. A recruiter approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about Nvidia's top job, according to a person familiar with the process. These developments left investors assessing both equipment demand and the financing support that Nvidia's next leadership would provide to customers.

Anthropic advanced from marketing to reported IPO pricing at $83 a share, above its $70-$78 range, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's early Asia account put expected proceeds at at least $68 billion, or more than $94 billion including a $26 billion private placement, and reported an increased offering size. The new pricing result brought a substantial equity-financing development before the expected trading debut, while the cost of supplying computing capacity remained central to the company's longer-term economics.

In another private-market transaction, lenders supplied a $1.3 billion loan for L Catterton's acquisition of healthcare platform Fullscript, freeing a Morgan Stanley-led group from its underwriting commitments. Carlyle and Park Square Capital were set to take over coffee-machine maker Evoca as its debt burden increased. These were different uses of private capital: one replaced acquisition financing, while the other involved a prospective transfer of control to creditors.

Scientific Games supplied a particularly sharp borrower-level contrast after the U.S. fixed-income close. Its $800 million unsecured bond rose 3 cents to 36 cents on Wednesday as lenders received fuller earnings and cash information; its $2.1 billion term loan was little changed at 75. The Brookfield-backed lottery business reported September-quarter revenue of $268 million, down 10%, and adjusted EBITDA of $73 million, down nearly 32%, people familiar with the figures said. They attributed part of the shortfall to a $13 million one-off adjustment associated with delayed contracts. The company drew $40 million on its revolver to repurchase bonds and had $44 million of restricted cash alongside a $359 million revolving credit line. Greater clarity supported distressed debt prices even as the operating figures deteriorated.

## Europe Weighs Tightening Against Financial-Market Vulnerabilities

ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic sharpened his assessment of inflation's prospective breadth. A December rate increase was highly likely absent surprises, he said, while price pressure beyond energy would emerge next year as second-round effects arrived with a lag. He considered market expectations for further 2027 tightening reasonable, subject to meeting-by-meeting decisions. That assessment added a stronger view of the coming transmission of energy costs, with inflation running around twice the ECB's 2% target.

The ECB's Financial Stability Review identified a separate vulnerability in the ownership and financing of sovereign debt. Hedge funds had helped absorb issuance and improve liquidity, but their sensitivity to prices and financing conditions could amplify abrupt yield moves, including when sovereign fundamentals had not changed. Vujcic said five large firms dominated the European field and cited episodes in which rapid hedge-fund activity widened spreads before markets normalized.

The review also addressed growing AI exposure as technology companies gained weight in equity indices. Vujcic said a sharp equity correction would produce a 1-percentage-point decline in European personal consumption. He judged banks well placed to absorb shocks because of profits, capital and liquidity, while highlighting liquidity vulnerabilities and leverage among some nonbanks. The assessment placed resilient bank balance sheets beside potential instability in market-based finance.

Germany formally nominated Princeton economist Markus Brunnermeier to replace Isabel Schnabel on the ECB Executive Board, advancing the package discussed earlier in the week. Berlin intended him to take the chief-economist portfolio after Philip Lane's term ends in May. The coalition arrangement also opened the way for German backing of Pablo Hernandez de Cos as president, alongside French support. The German government said EU discussions would continue with a view to completing appointments by year-end. Christine Lagarde separately confirmed she would remain president until February 7 and said a World Economic Forum role was one possible subsequent option.

European insurers face a different structural change in their capacity to finance credit. Solvency II revisions taking effect January 30 could free €80 billion of regulatory capital against existing holdings, S&P Global Ratings estimated. Blackstone, Apollo and other managers are seeking allocations from an EU insurance sector with about €10 trillion of assets, particularly into CLOs, private investment-grade debt and other securitized investments.

The changes reduce capital requirements on some private-equity and senior structured-credit investments, in certain cases by more than half. Qualifying long-term equity holdings can receive a 22% charge, compared with 39% for ordinary listed shares and 49% for most private-equity and other unlisted investments. A parallel securitization package includes a preliminary agreement to reduce risk-weight floors on senior portions of certain structures to 5% from 10% for banks.

Implementation will depend on mandates, expertise, due diligence and matching less-liquid assets to insurance liabilities. Some of the largest insurers calculate requirements through internal models, limiting the direct effect of particular changes. MetLife Investment Management's Laila Kollmorgen noted that CLOs represent 15% of U.S. life insurers' investment books, while securitizations of all types account for less than 1% of EU insurers' portfolios. Europe had almost €1.3 trillion of securitizations outstanding at June-end, up 2.7% annually, according to AFME.

Regulators questioned the reduction in protection behind solvency ratios. EIOPA Chair Petra Hielkema warned that similar-looking ratios could rest on less actual capital and said relief was not intended simply for shareholder or management payouts. Competition from U.S. AI financing could also draw allocations away from European projects. Apollo's Diego De Giorgi estimated Europe's annual investment need at €1.4 trillion, compared with €800 billion in the Draghi report, emphasizing financing for defense and technology supply chains as well as large companies.

Alstom's latest balance-sheet update illustrated the more immediate constraints on an individual issuer. It reduced expectations for asset disposals, increasing analysts' expectations of a rights issue as it seeks around €2 billion of debt reduction by September 2027 to protect investment-grade ratings. Management ruled out selling the main signaling operation and viewed services and joint ventures as strategically important. Citi analysts expected a significant equity component, potentially as much as €1.5 billion. Shares fell as much as 9.6%. The proposed funding mix remained under review as delays and cost overruns on German train projects strained cash flow.

British housing showed another consequence of high financing costs. Official September data put inner-London prices down 7.2% annually at £621,491, the largest fall since August 2009, while the whole capital declined 3.5%. Westminster fell 18.5% and Kensington & Chelsea 15.6%. National prices rose 1.2%. Savills' Lucian Cook linked inner London's sensitivity to stretched price-to-income ratios, with taxes on expensive property adding pressure. Gilts nevertheless outperformed Treasuries Wednesday after inflation data broadly matched consensus but came below the Bank of England's forecast, according to Bloomberg; the two-year yield declined more than 6 basis points to 4.92% in its session account.

## Japan's Auction Exposes Superlong Demand Constraints

Japan's 20-year auction attracted weaker demand as investors weighed rate volatility and the government's financing plans. Bid-to-cover fell to 3.64 from 5.84 at the previous sale, below the 12-month average of 3.92. The gap between the average and lowest accepted prices widened to 0.29 from 0.07, the largest in a year. The 20-year yield still declined 3 basis points on the day to 3.74%, while remaining more than 20 basis points higher for November.

BNP Paribas Asset Management strategist Ryutaro Kimura linked reluctance to buy superlong debt to reduced risk appetite amid volatile interest rates. He expected investors to await December's budget proposal for clarity on next fiscal year's issuance. Financing for higher defense expenditure and a proposed two-year food consumption-tax reduction remained important uncertainties for supply.

A draft Fiscal System Council recommendation warned that long average debt maturity and a large stock of low-coupon bonds provided time before higher rates fully affected interest payments, while urging fiscal consolidation before that impact arrived. The Finance Ministry had requested a record ¥16.6 trillion for interest payments next fiscal year. The panel sought consistent progress in debt sustainability and opposed financing the defense buildup through additional borrowing. Its warning concerned the market confidence required to sustain the government's investment agenda.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda maintained the case for further rate increases as economic, inflation and financial conditions warranted. On the proposed food-tax reduction, he said greater real purchasing power would likely support growth, while its effect on underlying inflation depended on business pricing and household behavior. The BOJ would incorporate the policy once details were finalized.

Ueda also distinguished emergency purchases to address serious market-functioning disruption from operations aimed at capping long-term yields. Investors could regard yield suppression as monetary financing of government spending, he warned, potentially increasing long-yield volatility. That distinction gave the auction and fiscal debate an important monetary-policy boundary as the BOJ continued its normalization process.

October trade figures provided fresh evidence of external support and import-cost pressure. Exports increased 20.5% annually, above the 20.0% Reuters consensus and September's 16.5%, reaching a record nominal value near ¥11.8 trillion. Shipments to the U.S. rose 23.9% and those to China 13.3%, with semiconductor-related AI demand contributing. Economists also identified higher selling prices and cost pass-through as contributors to nominal growth.

Imports rose 21.6%, below the expected 25.8%, to a record near ¥12.2 trillion, although volumes declined about 0.2%. The trade deficit was ¥476.5 billion against expectations for ¥956 billion. Elevated crude and transport costs helped explain the import bill. The smaller-than-expected deficit and strong export receipts therefore accompanied a continuing energy-cost burden, with recent domestic consumption weakness still relevant to the BOJ's growth assessment.

## Currency Defense and Public Borrowing Follow Different Paths

Bank Indonesia raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 6%, its first increase since June, against a final Bloomberg survey in which 22 of 38 economists expected a hold. Governor Destry Damayanti said the move aimed to stabilize the rupiah and preemptively keep inflation within the 1.5%-3.5% target range. The currency edged up less than 0.1% to 18,238 per dollar after the decision, while the 10-year government yield extended its increase to 7.75%.

The bank combined the increase with further reductions in hedging premiums on certain domestic nondeliverable forwards. It plans cross-currency repo transactions by March at the latest, allowing banks to obtain liquidity against eligible BI dollar securities. Destry said lower reserve requirements and macroprudential incentives would support financing to the real economy alongside the tighter policy rate.

Danamon's Irman Faiz cited credit growth above 13%, with consumer lending up 4.7%, as evidence of resilience and forecast another quarter-point increase in December to 6.25%, followed by a hold through 2027. GDP grew around 5.5% annually in Q3. Currency pressures included the stronger dollar, MSCI's downgrade warning and domestic political uncertainty, leaving the central bank balancing exchange-rate stability with growth.

South Africa's fresh inflation figures complicated that same balance. October consumer inflation accelerated to 5.2% from 4.5%, matching the Bloomberg median, while core inflation rose to 4.2% from 4%. The rand fell as much as 1.9% during the session, reaching its weakest since March as gold declined and anticipated Fed increases threatened its yield advantage. The benchmark 10-year government yield rose about 9 basis points to 8.91%, a four-week high.

Most surveyed economists still expected the South African Reserve Bank to hold at 7.25% Thursday. Ninety One's James Turp judged the inflation result insufficiently above expectations to require tightening, while acknowledging the firmer core reading. The Financial and Fiscal Commission separately described a proposed framework requiring successive administrations to produce credible medium-term fiscal plans, independently assessed and subject to parliamentary accountability. The principles-based approach would seek durable consolidation through three-year planning periods, rather than a fixed debt ceiling.

Chile reported a larger growth setback: Q3 GDP fell 1.8% from Q2, against a 1.4% decline expected, and 1.1% annually. Mining contracted 12.9% quarterly and the rest of the economy 0.2%. The central bank revised Q2 growth to 0.1% from a previously slightly negative figure rounded to zero. That revision altered the sequence of quarterly activity behind earlier recession descriptions.

Severe weather interrupted mines and transport, while unemployment and fuel costs weighed on confidence. Pantheon Macroeconomics' Andrés Abadía expected much of next year's recovery to reflect favorable comparisons, with lower ore grades and weak investment constraining mining. Inflation at 4.5% remained above the 3% target. Congress approved a fuel-price cap through April this week, adding a new policy response as the economy faced both weaker output and elevated costs.

Mexico's sovereign sustainable-debt issuance reached 169.3 billion pesos, or $9.1 billion, up 79% from full-year 2025 and a record since its first such government bond in 2020, according to the country's sustainable-finance council. Pension funds with about $500 billion in assets were important buyers. New disclosure requirements encourage sustainability reporting without obliging them to purchase ESG securities.

Demand offered a clearer benefit than a consistent pricing discount. Bloomberg's comparison of two sustainable and conventional bond pairs in the same currency and maturity year found sustainable yields 5 basis points higher in one case and 1 basis point higher in the other. VALMEX's Yazmín Matus said the advantage lay in volumes demanded. An earlier combined 35 billion-peso sustainable fixed- and floating-rate sale drew 2.6 times coverage, compared with 1.7 times for a separate 9 billion-peso Udibonos offering.

Citi's Miguel Azevedo projected more African sovereign dollar-bond transactions in 2027 than the record 25 so far this year. Nine countries had raised $16.9 billion in eurobonds, while African companies excluding development banks had raised almost $10 billion through 89 sales, Bloomberg data showed. Azevedo attributed the pipeline to improving macroeconomic stability and reforms, with the IMF projecting sub-Saharan growth of 4.5% this year and next. His forecast described prospective issuance from a market that had retained access through global turbulence.

Kenya disclosed a more constrained use of financing proceeds. Treasury Secretary John Mbadi said much of the money from Vodacom's additional Safaricom stake and the securitization of future dividends was invested in government bonds and bills while an appeal proceeded. The transactions raised 204.3 billion shillings and 40.2 billion shillings respectively. A high court ordered the additional 20% stake returned to the Treasury two months earlier; the case is before the Court of Appeal. Mbadi said the appeal court had not barred use of the money, while the Treasury warned that the dispute threatened the intended National Infrastructure Fund capital base.

In U.S. municipals, a new Bloomberg analysis showed Texas voters rejected at least $7 billion of bond propositions this month, including at least $6 billion for schools. Collin County's $817 million package failed even though the supporting tax rate was not due to rise; officials said ballot language warning of a tax increase may have contributed. Bexar County voters rejected San Antonio ISD's $600 million package and a roughly 3-cent property-tax increase. The district said future building renovations or replacements depended on eventual bond approval, with enrollment declines and a structural budget deficit already constraining finances. Plano's rejection of venue taxes also forced reassessment of the proposed financing for a Dallas Stars arena.

## Forward Market Significance

Anthropic's expected November 19 trading debut will test public-market demand after the reported $83 pricing and expanded fundraising. The immediate question is how the shares trade as Nvidia's earnings-led rebound has already faded, while investors assess the industry's computing costs and access to both debt and equity. Supplier investment discipline and actual financing execution remain distinct determinants of how rapidly infrastructure can expand.

South Africa's Thursday policy decision follows the 5.2% inflation reading, higher core inflation and renewed currency pressure. A hold at the expected 7.25% would leave the bank relying on existing restraint as it evaluates exchange-rate effects and declining oil. Indonesia's next decision follows a different starting point after its surprise increase, with domestic credit resilience and continued rupiah stability central to whether further tightening follows.

The December 8-9 FOMC meeting now carries a more explicit choice over pace and communication. Waller's condition for splitting a half-point adjustment across meetings puts the credibility of January guidance alongside incoming inflation. Daly's measured approach leaves greater weight on uncertainty over investment, tariffs and the war. The next inflation observations will determine whether support for additional tightening translates into a larger immediate step or successive smaller increases.

Japan's December budget proposal will reveal the issuance consequences of fiscal plans that weighed on the 20-year auction. The BOJ's December 18 decision remains a separate policy event, with Ueda's assessment of demand and underlying inflation relevant to further normalization. In Europe, leaders' consideration of the ECB appointments next week will determine whether the German nomination and political backing produce an agreed leadership package.

October's final U.S. building-permit estimate is scheduled for November 25 at 13:00 GMT, with Trading Economics showing a 1.295 million consensus. It will revisit the sharp preliminary contraction in the pipeline after starts rebounded and pending purchases fell. Separately, summit diplomacy in Shenzhen leaves changes to technology access and regional security unresolved. Any concrete agreement affecting advanced computing or energy transport would change financing assumptions that remain exposed to both policy restrictions and physical supply risks.

overall_summary.headline: Cheaper oil leads a longer-dated Treasury rally as Fed tightening expectations hold
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their recovery as cheaper oil eased inflation compensation and intraday technology-share weakness supported demand for government debt. The 10-year yield fell 3.85 basis points to 5.0683% and the 30-year declined 4.81 basis points to 5.4099%; the 2-year edged up 0.01 basis point to 4.8042%. The 2- to 10-year spread narrowed 3.86 basis points to 26.41. A 3-basis-point fall in the 10-year breakeven accounted for most of the nominal yield decline, alongside a 0.85-basis-point reduction in the real yield. Real financing costs remained higher over the week and month.

October's Fed minutes showed almost all participants expected further increases. Christopher Waller argued that a 50-basis-point December move could be needed unless guidance credibly signaled consecutive 25-basis-point steps; Mary Daly favored further tightening at a measured pace. Rising oil inventories helped relieve energy-price pressure as that policy debate kept short-term borrowing costs elevated.

U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed, while Proofpoint completed nearly $2 billion of financing on improved terms. Credit managers described growing refinancing pressure and competition for capital from AI investment. Japan's weak 20-year auction and Indonesia's surprise increase to 6% showed that financing conditions remained uneven across markets.
